artworks.medium: Graphite with white chalk.
artworks.description: Watermark: none. A student of Ingres, Chasseriau adopted the characteristic style of his master's portrait drawings. In this graphite sketch, Chasseriau shows the wife of his close friend and fellow artist Charles Damour casually seated against the arm of a chair. At the lower right, Chasseriau dedicated the portrait to Damour. -- Exhibition Label, from "Life Lines: Portrait Drawings from Dürer to Picasso."

The large sheet was likely done in the winter of 1785, after the Maison du Roi had identified twelve history painters who would be given commissions for the next Salon of 1787. David was included in the group who were to paint scenes from antiquity. As was his custom, he elaborated an ambitious and…

artworks.description: Degas often experimented by mixing drawing media and printmaking techniques. In this case, he first produced a monotype of two singers on stage seen from behind with a view to the audience--a perspective that exploits the intimacy and the proximity to performers that Degas (and other wealthy patrons) enjoyed through privileged behind-the-scenes access. Degas then enlivened the general, slightly abstracted forms of the print with richly colored pastels. The two popular singers depicted here, E…

artworks.description: Watermark: none. Using dark washes of thinned oil paint to throw the figure into relief, Degas expertly appropriated the tone of the paper itself to highlight the dancer's back. This sheet is one of five surviving studies related to the artist's canvas Dance Class at the Opéra on the Rue le Peletier (1872; Musée d'Orsay, Paris). Typical of Degas's dynamic working method, the figure does not correspond exactly to her appearance in the final painting. -- Exhibition Label, from "Drawn to Great…

artworks.title: Forest View with an Oak Tree
artworks.medium: Watercolor with yellow opaque watercolor over black chalk.
artworks.description: Watermark: none. Delacroix was heralded as a master storyteller and a history painter with a vivid imagination and an innovative sense of color. Although revered as the last painter of the grand manner, he was not widely considered a painter of nature. Inveterate draftsman that he was, however, he produced a number of studies of the natural world that are striking in their beauty and depth of feeling, such as this view of an asymmetrically foliated oak tree on a hillside. -- Exhibition Label,…

artworks.title: Mephistopheles Appears Before Faust
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and wash over graphite.
artworks.description: An often overlooked or underrated aspect of Delacroix's work is his accomplishments as a book illustrator. The well-read artist counted many writers among his closest friends, and it is no surprise that the artist would have been drawn to Goethe's Faust and its moral complexity. The luxury book publishing industry flourished during the nineteenth century. Like many artists of his day, Delacroix frequently contributed to such volumes in the form of drawings for illustrations. Also, since he wa…

artworks.title: She Talks with Her Cat (Habla con su gato)

artworks.description: Marcel Roethlisberger surmised that this sheet is probably from a sketchbook of nature studies dating to the early 1630s. Leaves from the dismembered sketchbook are found in several collections, with considerable portions preserved in the British Museum and the Royal Library, Windsor. Among the subjects found in the presumed sketchbook are identifiable medieval or antique monuments which Claude likely drew onsite. The coastal town depicted here, however, has not yet been identified.

Roethlisberger described this sheet as a landscape with St. John, though it is hard to discern whether the reclining figure holds a staff with a cross. The composition is not connected to other known drawings or paintings and its combination of chalk and wash indicate it likely dates to the 1660s.

artworks.description: Collins is a new name for the drawings collection. Known primarily for his coastal views of England, Collins also traveled to the continent for study and inspiration. artworks.description: Marie Spartali began her career as a model for members of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood and for photographer Julia Margaret Cameron, but soon decided to become a painter herself. After marrying fellow artist W. James Stillman, Spartali spent part of her time in Italy, between Florence and Rome. The Ponte Nomentano is a picturesque Roman bridge celebrated for its medieval bridge tower, seen at left in Stillman's watercolor. She enjoyed a long career although her work has remained little known.

artworks.title: Nightclub in New York
artworks.medium: Pen and ink and watercolor on laid paper.
artworks.description: Beckmann, who is best known for his large allegorical paintings, was forced to leave Germany in 1937 after Hitler declared his work "degenerate." This drawing, which he created after relocating from Amsterdam to New York, presents a tense view of the relationship between the sexes. For Beckmann, acrobats and clowns were not merely subjects of entertainment. They symbolized the fate of man caught between comedy and tragedy.

artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and wash, red chalk wash, white chalk with wet brush, over black chalk.
artworks.description: No fewer than twelve figures--including the Christ child--and eight farmyard animals inhabit Boucher's luminous Nativity. Inspired by the pastorals of the Italian artist Giovanni Benedetto Castiglione, this autonomous drawing is executed in a complex and layered mixed-media technique. artworks.title: A View of Tangier from the Southeast
artworks.medium: Watercolor and pen and brown ink over black chalk on two joined sheets of paper.
artworks.description: Hollar accompanied an English delegation to the key Moroccan port of Tangier as a royal scenographer charged with making accurate views of the city. Although Portugal had ceded Tangier to England in 1662, the English were unable to wrest control of the city from Sultan al-Rashīd (r. 1664-72). The delegation failed even to negotiate trading rights, but once back in England, the artist made a successful series of etchings of the city based on drawings such as this one. -- Exhibition Label, fro…

artworks.medium: Watercolor, over graphite, on paper.
artworks.description: The inscription along the bottom of this watercolor, while hard to decipher, seems to indicate the artist's appreciation for the sitter's colorful garments. The words "orange" and "violette" are legible and correspond to the man's long orange vest over a violet kaftan. Similar figures appear in Fromentin's paintings of the 1850s. The large white turban suggests the sitter may be an Ottoman Turk, although such head coverings were common throughout North Africa.

artworks.medium: Brush and black ink with white opaque watercolor on paper.
artworks.description: An avid draftsman and illustrator, Forain focused on the denizens of Paris and their activities. This sheet is among his rare forays into portraying animals. Here, he's depicted a common sight on the city's streets: two horses yoked to a cart. Such teams were used by tradespeople and farmers to move goods quickly. The horses have paused, and Forain is more interested in their forms and shadows than what is transported in the cart. On the verso of mount in black chalk, four studies of mouths.

artworks.description: Kirchner was a leading figure of the Brücke (Bridge) group of German Expressionist artists. He considered drawing the medium that best expressed his conception of art as a direct, spontaneous experience. He may have made this abbreviated drawing of a landscape with a tower in the distance along the Elbe River near Dresden. Landscape remained an important subject for Kirchner throughout his life, and especially during his final decades in Switzerland.

This drawing, executed in a bright palette of pastel, features a wall overgrown with foliage along a Mediterranean seascape. artworks.title: Partial Eclipse
artworks.medium: Collage of cut and torn printed and colored papers with watercolor.
artworks.description: California artist William Dole is best-known for his collages, which he began making while living in Florence in the mid-1950s. By 1958 it had become his major medium. His collages, such as this one, typically mix various types of papers, often including Japanese paper. "Partial Eclipse" is typical of the artist's style in its geometric composition and its inclusion of printed text. Dole believed that words created a kind of visual energy unattainable by purely abstract forms and color.

artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for an engraving illustrating the second story of the fourth day in an edition of Boccaccio's “Decamerone” published in Paris by Prault in 1757-61 (the image is captioned: IV Journée, Nouvelle 2). The scene depicts the public humiliation of Fra Alberto as he is exhibited in the piazza in the guise of a wild man.

artworks.title: Drawing for the Decamerone (v Journée, Nouvelle 6)
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink, brown ink and wash, with traces of red chalk, on paper mounted on card.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for an engraving illustrating the sixth story of the fifth day in an edition of Boccaccio's “Decamerone” published in Paris by Prault in 1757-61 (the image is captioned: V Journée, Nouvelle 6). The scene shows the lovers Restituta and Gianni of Procida bound at the stake.

artworks.title: Headpiece for Canto I of Alessandro Tassoni's "Secchia rapita"
artworks.medium: Pen and ink and pencil on paper, mounted on paper backing.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for a decorative headpiece for the opening of Canto I (p. 1) of an edition of Alessandro Tassoni's “Secchia rapita” (“The Stolen Bucket”), published in Paris by L. Prault and P. Durand in 1766. Tassoni's mock-heroic poem, originally published in Paris in 1622, blends the construct of an epic with an absurd premise: a 14th century war between Modena and Bologna was actually caused by the Modenese stealing a bucket from Bologna.

artworks.title: Cascade at Rydal
artworks.medium: Pencil on paper.
artworks.description: Title from pencil inscription at upper right. The finished painting of the same subject, entitled "Rydal waterfall" and signed and dated 1795 by the artist, is in the collection of the Derby Museum & Art Gallery. Cf. B. Nicolson. Joseph Wright of Derby : painter of light. New York : Pantheon Books, 1968, v. 1 p. 93, 94, 267 & v. 2 plate 352.

artworks.title: Langdale Pikes from Lowood
artworks.medium: Pencil on paper.
artworks.description: Title from inscription in ink at upper left. A painting by Wright of the same subject, with the addition of a figure pushing off a boat in the foreground, is recorded as a lost painting by Nicolson, who reproduces a painting of Lake Windermere with Langdale Pikes answering this description which he identifies as a copy after Wright; this same painting, newly reattributed to Wright, was later sold at Sotheby's in London on June 7, 2006 (Sale L06120, Lot 187).

artworks.title: Birches
artworks.medium: Pencil on paper.
artworks.description: Although he is also a painter, Kipniss is perhaps best known as a printmaker, whose mezzotints in particular have a characteristic sharpness and intensity. His drawings are rendered in the same exacting style. Kipniss's imagery is restricted to the exploration of woods and solitary trees, houses and yards, interiors and windows, chairs and vases. "Birches" was drawn from the artist's imagination and not from direct observation. It is an autonomous work as well as a study for an oil painting.

artworks.description: A major post-war American artist, Conner was active in San Francisco as a sculptor, draftsman, and filmmaker from the late 1950s on. In 1975, he began his first sustained experiments with inkblots, intricate fields of glyphs inspired by his memories of childhood ink spills. The inkblot became his primary drawing technique in the last two decades of his life.

artworks.title: Portrait of a Man
artworks.medium: Red chalk on paper.
artworks.description: The identity of the artist who made this drawing remains unconfirmed, though it is usually attributed to Jean-Marc Nattier, a successful painter of court society during the reign of Louis XV. Nattier was received into the Académie Royale as a history painter, yet his financial situation pushed him in the direction of portraiture, a field in which he could more easily support his large family. Rendered in red chalk, the drawing appears to be a portrait study of a contemporary of the artist.

artworks.description: Juel was the foremost Danish portraitist of his day, and was appointed court painter in 1780. During the next forty years, he produced a large number of elegant yet remarkably unidealized portraits of royal, aristocratic, and bourgeois sitters. artworks.description: In his sketchbook studies, Delacroix often drew in pencil, adding notes about color, texture, and details of clothing and lighting. In many of these sheets, he drew architectural decoration and ornament, as well as figures, textiles, and everyday objects of North African design. In this page from one of his dismembered sketchbooks that document his time in Morocco, his keen eye generated a flurry of quick studies. artworks.title: Nasturtium
artworks.medium: Watercolor and opaque watercolor over black chalk, on laid paper.
artworks.description: Withoos trained as a painter and specialized in depictions of plants, animals, and insects in watercolor and oil. This vibrant study of a nasturtium is a great example of her style of botanical drawing, which was admired by contemporary Dutch horticulturalists and botanists, including Agnes Block (1629-1704). Withoos skillfully layered transparent and opaque watercolor washes to describe the fiery striped petals and convey the color and texture of nasturtium's distinctive shield-shaped leaves…

artworks.medium: Charcoal on paper.
artworks.description: French artist Anne-Marie Schneider compares her drawing practice to the writing of a diary. In a cartoon style that recalls the work of Jean Dubuffet and Philip Guston she explores a variety of human encounters, exposing the relationship between mental universe and exterior world. Her drawings are inspired from everyday experience as well as literature and political events. In the present work she evokes on a mode at once absurd and tragic, the terror of a schizophrenic bus passenger.

artworks.medium: Watercolor and pen and black ink on wove paper.
artworks.dimensions: 18 7/8 x 24 13/16 inches (48 x 63 cm); in decorative frame: 26 7/8 x 31 7/8 x 1 7/8 inches
artworks.description: André Masson was a key figure of the Surrealist movement from its beginning in France in the 1920s. His early contribution to the movement consisted of 'automatic' drawings, a spontaneous style of drawing characterized by free-form gestures. In the late thirties Masson adopted a more controlled and figurative mode in subjects often inspired by mythology. "Ville cranienne" is an example of Masson's second phase of Surrealism. artworks.title: Portrait of Philibert-Emmanuel de Beaumanoir de Lavardin
artworks.medium: Black chalk, pastel, watercolor, white opaque watercolor, on three joined sheets of paper.
artworks.description: Nanteuil was a prolific engraver at the court of Louis XIV. This is his preparatory study, drawn from life, for a portrait print of the bishop Philibert-Emmanuel de Beaumanoir de Lavardin (1617-1671). The bishop is shown at age forty-three, wearing a skullcap and a clerical band around his neck. Despite his profession, Lavardin was not known to be a very devout man; indeed, he spent the 1660s trying to ward off criticism that he was atheist. artworks.description: This watercolor is a strong example of Martin's epic approach to historical subject matter. Its protagonist is the Greek philosopher Diogenes of Sinope, who made a virtue of the simple life, begging for a living and residing in a barrel. He likened himself to a dog, hence the name of the school of thought he came to define: Cynicism (Gr. kynikos = "dog-like"). The episode depicted is the story of how he came to a pool intending to drink, using a cup. When he saw a child drinking from his hand…

artworks.title: Family of Darius Before Alexander
artworks.medium: Brown ink over red chalk, on paper.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for an illustration probably intended for Charles Rollin's "The ancient history of the Egyptians, Carthaginians, Assyrians, Babylonians, Medes and Persians, Macedonians, and Grecians" (first published in London: Knapton, 1738-1740). The scene depicts the mother of the defeated Darius kneeling at the feet of Hephaestion and Alexander, with the rest of Darius' family grouped behind her.

artworks.title: Antiochus and Stratonice
artworks.medium: Brown ink over red chalk, on paper.

The scene shows an interior with Erasistratos (or Seleucus I?) at right, pointing to Antiochus lying sick in bed while addressing queen Stratonice, who stands on the right with her servants.

artworks.title: Two Medals
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink over graphite, on paper.
artworks.description: Gravelot designed this armorial device with two medals for the engraved title vignette to Volume III of Maximilien de Béthune (1560-1641), duke de Sully's "Mémoires" (London : 1747). One medal features a bee surmounted by a crown, the other bears a crown above laurel branches; below, a putto is seated alongside a pair of dogs and holding a rudder. Gravelot also designed the three headpiece vignettes which depict scenes from the career of the author, who served as minister to Henry IV of Fra…

artworks.medium: Pen and black ink over graphite, on paper; verso rubbed with black chalk.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is likely preparatory for a medal or the lid of a snuffbox. The vignette depicts four figures in a circular border illustrating Aesop's fable of the father teaching his sons the lesson of the bundle of sticks, with "Concordia Victrix" above, and the date 1767 in Roman numerals (M.DCC.LXVII) below. The drawing is squared for transfer to another support and the letters a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h appear in the grid along the upper margin. A related drawing in black chalk showing th…

St. Louis is depicted seated with the five “Saracens” (a Christian term for Arab Muslims) kneeling around him at his feet. The Morgan preserves a second design by Gravelot, also engraved by Lemire, for this publication (Acc. No. 1963.13:6). artworks.title: Minerva Seated on Clouds, Surrounded by Four Putti

artworks.description: Gravelot's sketch is preliminary for an engraved head-piece vignette in Jean Baptiste Bourguignon d'Anville's "Notice de l'Ancienne Gaule" (Paris : 1760). Jean Baptiste Bourguignon d'Anville (1697-1782) was Gravelot's older brother and a well-known geographer; the artist designed several illustrations and maps for his brother's treatises, including this important volume. Minerva is shown seated on a cloud with a shield, surrounded by four putti. The engraving after the drawing by Noel Le Mire…

artworks.title: Scene of Sacrifice
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink over graphite, on paper; verso rubbed with black chalk.
artworks.description: Gravelot's sketch was probably intended for an engraved illustration to Abbé Jean Raymond de Petity's "Les Voeux de la France et de l'Empire...." (Paris : 1770). The sheet contains a medallion design with a priest preparing to sacrifice a bull as a figure is tortured on a pyre in the background and a group of figures celebrate around an altar on a mountaintop. The Morgan preserves two further designs for Petity's publication: see 1963.13:19 and 1968.15:39.

A funeral monument is shown surmounted by an urn and flanked by two grieving female figures and cupids. See also 1963.13:17.

According to Kraemer, this drawing and 1963.13:11 “show two different stages in the artist's work…

Two allegorical female figures representing Prudence and the City of Paris are shown in front of the burning opera house. The figure of Paris is seated in an attitude of despair as Prudence gestures towards a pump and barrel. The inspiration for the design was evidently the destruction by fire of the great…

artworks.title: "Guy Fawkes & Catesby Landing the Powder", with additional sketches in margins
artworks.medium: Watercolor and graphite, on paper.
artworks.description: Title from item. Sketch by Cruikshank for a frontispiece illustration for v. I of William Harrison Ainsworth's novel, Guy Fawkes, or, The gunpowder treason (London : Richard Bentley, 1841).

artworks.title: Guy Fawkes and Humphrey Chetham Rescuing Father Oldcorne and Viviana Radcliffe from the Pursuivant

artworks.description: Title from Ray. Sketch by Cruikshank for an illustration for William Harrison Ainsworth's novel, Guy Fawkes, or, The gunpowder treason (London : Richard Bentley, 1841).

artworks.description: Six sketches on single sheet, with four on recto and two on verso.

artworks.title: French Brandy
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink and watercolor, on paper.
artworks.description: Title from published illustration. Drawing by Cruikshank for No. LXXXVIII of the Gallery of comicalities (London, n.d.); published illustration accompanied by verses with the first line reading, "Ah ha, Mr. Enghshman ! voyez ici, De grandest specific to banish ennui"; caricature also published by George Goodger in his The gallery of 140 comicalities (London, 1831).

artworks.title: English Beer
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink and watercolor, on paper.
artworks.description: Title from published illustration. Drawing by Cruikshank for No. LXXXVII of the Gallery of comicalities (London, n.d.); published illustration accompanied by verses entitled "Heavy wet", with the first line reading, "King William and Reform, I say, In such a case who can be neuter ?"; caricature also published by George Goodger in his The gallery of 140 comicalities, under the title "Heavy wet" (London, 1831).

artworks.title: Gourmand
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink and watercolor, on paper.
artworks.description: Drawing by Cruikshank, probably intended for an illustration for an unidentified publication.

artworks.title: The Opening of the Great Industrial Exhibition of All Nations
artworks.medium: Graphite and watercolor on paper.
artworks.description: Title from published print. Preliminary sketch by Cruikshank, being a detail of a design for an etched print published in London by David Bogue in 1851.

artworks.title: Family of Sheep
artworks.medium: Watercolor on paper.

artworks.medium: Pen and black ink and black chalk, on paper.
artworks.description: This design is one of four preparatory drawings by Gravelot in the Morgan's collection intended for an engraved frontispiece executed by Jean Charles Le Vasseur for Henri Panckoucke's "Lettre de don Carlos à Elisabeth" (Paris : Panckoucke et Veuve Duchesne, 1768). Don Carlos is shown standing beside a table as the guards enter at left to take him to his execution; he holds up a miniature portrait in one hand and his other hand rests on the table top, gripping a letter. Of the four studies, t…

artworks.title: In this "Style" 1/s - Result, "Disappointment."
artworks.medium: Graphite on paper.
artworks.description: Title from item. Original drawing for a cartoon, possibly intended for publication in an unidentified periodical. Removed from an album of drawings compiled by former owner Frederick Smallfield.

artworks.title: Design for a Title Page to a Book of Poetry(?)
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and brown and gray wash over graphite, touched with white chalk, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design probably was intended to serve as title page illustration although a related publication has yet to be identified. A male figure is shown seated in the foreground at right, flanked by two putti; a circular temple with a statue appears in the background, with a bust of a man on a pedestal, surrounded by flying putti, at left.

artworks.title: Allegory of Geometry(?)
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink and wash, with white and red chalk for toning, on tan paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design probably was intended to serve as a vignette or tailpiece illustration to a work on geometry or philosophy. A rocaille cartouche contains a female figure who holds a compass to the bust of a man mounted on a pyramid and supports a tablet bearing a triangle and circle with her left hand.

artworks.title: La Trémoille and Arondel Find their Mistresses at La Sainte-Beaume
artworks.medium: Black chalk, with single rule of red chalk parallel to upper margin, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for an engraved frontispiece to Chant IX of Voltaire's “La Pucelle d'Orléans” (Genève : Cramer, 1762; facing p. 159). The scene depicts Arondel and La Tremoille and their mistresses sitting in a landscape; beyond, at left, are a group of praying monks while St Mary Magdalene appears on a cloud in the upper left corner. See also 1968.15:34-36 for further preparatory drawings by Gravelot for the same publication.

artworks.title: Fight in the Streets of Orléans
artworks.medium: Black chalk on paper.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for an engraved frontispiece to Chant XV of Voltaire's “La Pucelle d'Orléans” (Genève : Cramer,1762; facing p. 262). The drawing shows only the lower half of the finished composition, with a soldier driving back a crowd of people in the streets of Orléans and the houses above only faintly sketched in. See also 1968.15:28, 1968.15:35, and 1968.15:36 for additional preparatory drawings by Gravelot for the same publication.

artworks.title: Scene of Sorcery
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink, with touches of black and white chalk, on paper; lightly incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for an engraved frontispiece to the “Satyrae” in a 1770 English edition of Horace's works (“Opera of Horace”, Birmingham : John Baskerville, 1770; p. 187). The sketch illustrates a scene from Book I, 8th Satire, verses 23-50, in which the witches Canidia and Sagana summon the spirits of the dead by pouring the blood of a black lamb into a trench in front of a statue of Priapus. The figure of Priapus is shown holding a scythe, and two small additional figures k…

artworks.title: Hilaritas Universa
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink over graphite, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for an engraved medallion entitled "Hilaritas Universa", illustrating Abbé Jean Raymond de Petity's "Les Voeux de la France et de l'Empire..." (Paris : 1770; p. v). This decoratively framed oval drawing shows a seated goddess regarding herself in a mirror, flanked by two putti; in the background, figures are shown variously seated at a table and dancing in a ring in the countryside. The engraving was executed by Pierre Chenu. The Abbé de Petity was the Queen…

artworks.title: Allegory of Poetry(?) II
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design has not been related to an illustration appearing in a published volume. The classical figure of a woman is shown standing with a palm of wreath in her right hand and her left hand raised in a dramatic gesture; she is surrounded by symbols of sacred and heroic poetry, and Pegasus is shown on the wing at upper left. See 1968.15:37 for a related drawing, as yet unconnected to a publication.

artworks.title: Allegory of Poetry(?)
artworks.medium: Black chalk on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design has not been related to an illustration appearing in a published volume. The classical figure of a woman is shown standing with a palm or wreath in her right hand and her left hand raised in a dramatic gesture; she is surrounded by symbols of sacred and heroic poetry, and Pegasus is shown on the wing at upper left. See 1968.15:38 for a related drawing, as yet unconnected to a publication.

artworks.title: Death of La Trémoille and Dorothée
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink, on brown tracing paper.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for an engraved frontispiece to Chant XVIII of Voltaire's “La Pucelle d'Orléans” (Genève : Cramer, 1762; facing p. 311). The scene depicts the death of La Trémoille and Dorothée, with the distressed young knight standing beside the dead body of Dorothée and throwing himself on his sword, while a second knight stands watching aghast on the left; a chapel appears in the background at left. See also 1968.15:28, 1968.15:34, and 1968.15:35 for additional prepa…

artworks.title: Death of La Trémoille and Dorothée II
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink and black chalk, on paper.

artworks.title: Apollo(?) Seated Surrounded by Several Figures
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink and black chalk, on blue paper; partially incised with stylus.
artworks.description: According to Ruth Kraemer, Gravelot's design "is possibly intended for a vignette or headpiece in a book of poetry. There is another, slightly more finished drawing of the same composition, also on the Roederer mount, at the Houghton Library, Harvard University, Cambridge, Mass." A seated classical male figure is shown flanked by two female figures, one of whom appears to be Venus; he extends his hand to Cupid, who stands in front of him; at left, additional female figures are shown seated on…

artworks.title: Laissez faire mon fils II
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink over graphite, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's drawing is preparatory for an engraved frontispiece to Act IV of Beaumarchais' five-act play “Eugénie” (Paris : Merlin, 1767). This study depicts a less developed stage of Gravelot's composition than 1968.15:26. The title is inscribed twice at the bottom, indicating the artist's intention of extending the foot of the design. Several figures are shown gathered in a room; at center a gentleman armed with a sword rushes towards a man standing at left, as two other men attempt to inte…

artworks.title: Laissez faire mon fils
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink over graphite, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's drawing is preparatory for an engraved frontispiece to Act IV of Beaumarchais' five act play “Eugénie” (Paris : Merlin, 1767). Several figures are shown gathered in a room; at center a gentleman armed with a sword rushes towards a man standing on the left, as two other men attempt to intercede. See 1968.15:27 for another preparatory drawing by Gravelot for this scene, which was ultimately engraved by Jean Charles Le Vasseur (1734-1816).

artworks.title: Bearded Male Figure, Standing, Conversing with a Crowned Woman
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink over graphite, on paper.
artworks.description: Gravelot's drawing, with visible pentimenti, probably was preparatory for a book illustration, although it has not been connected to a publication. A bearded man is shown standing before a seated and crowned woman, at whom he gestures or points with his left hand. This may represent Haman before Esther.

artworks.title: Historical Scene
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink and wash over graphite, with white chalk, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design probably was intended to serve as an illustration for an unidentified publication. A king and his retinue are greeted by an old man and two soldiers in front of a palace with columns.

artworks.title: Several Figures in a Church(?) Interior
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink over graphite, with red chalk, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design probably was intended to serve as an illustration for an unidentified publication. Three men and a woman are shown standing in an aisle, with a fifth figure of a woman occupying one of the benches or pews at right.

artworks.title: Je ne puis plus soutenir le supplice où je suis
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink over graphite, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for an engraved frontispiece to Act II of Beaumarchais' five-act play “Eugénie” (Paris : Merlin, 1767). Two men, Captain Cowerly and Baron Hartley, are in lively conversation while two women, Eugénie and Madame Murer, are speaking more intimately in an elegant interior. The engraving after the drawing was executed by Louis Joseph Masquelier (1741-1811).

artworks.title: Otez vous de mes yeux. Vous m'avez rendu le plus miserable des hommes
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink over graphite, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for an engraved frontispiece to Act III of Beaumarchais' five-act play “Eugénie” (Paris : Merlin, 1767). Eugénie is shown attempting to embrace her father the Baron, who stands distraught with his arms raised; behind them stands the concerned figure of Madame Murer. The engraving after the drawing was executed by Antoine-Jean Duclos (1742-1795).

artworks.title: Je vous la donne
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink over graphite, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's drawing is preparatory for an engraved frontispiece to Act V of Beaumarchais' five-act play “Eugénie” (Paris : Merlin, 1767). The play's principal characters are assembled in an elegant interior: Baron Hartley, at right, takes the hand of the Earl who kneels before him, gesturing at the same time towards his daughter, who sits or kneels at left, supported by her aunt, Madame Murer. The engraving was executed by Jean Jacques André Le Veau (1729-1786).

artworks.title: The Emperor of Japan on His Throne II
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink and brown wash over black chalk, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for an illustration to Act III, Scene IV of Fenouillot de Falbaire de Quingey's tragedy “Les Jammabos, ou, Les Moines Japonais”, as published in his “Oeuvres” (Paris : Veuve Duchesne, 1787, facing p. 52). It is one of two preparatory drawings, along with 1963.13:14, for the illustration engraved by Charles Le Vasseur (1734-1816). artworks.title: Oh mon Perre!...ma Fille!...quoi c'est vous?
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink over graphite, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for a vignette enlivening the marquis de La Salle's comedy, "Histoire de Sophie Francourt" (Paris : Merlin, 1768; v. II, p. 102). A man and his young daughter are shown rushing into one another's arms. and signed at lower right The engraving after this drawing for the four-act comedy was executed by Jean Jacques Andre le Veau (1729-1786).

artworks.title: Allegorical Scene
artworks.medium: Black and red chalk on paper; partially traced with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design was probably intended for a book illustration, although no related publication can be identified.A classical female figure, perhaps signifying Prudence, is shown seated at a table with an hourglass in front of a curtain, writing on a scroll, with a snake and mirror at her feet. A large group of people fill a hall with a colonnade in the background, and there is a bust of a bearded man at the far right.

artworks.title: Murder Scene in a Palace
artworks.medium: Graphite on paper; partially incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design was probably intended for a book illustration, although no related publication has been identified. A woman in Turkish costume is shown brandishing a dagger as a man wearing a turban in front of her collapses or recoils against a column; another man in Roman dress restrains the woman as two male figures in Ottoman dress look on. According to Ruth Kraemer, “Figures in similar Turkish or Persian costumes are found in illustrations after Gravelot to the plays Bajazet and Esther…

artworks.title: Antiquities of Egypt
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink over graphite and red chalk, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for an engraved frontispiece to Volume I of Charles Rollin's “The Ancient History of the Egyptians, Carthaginians, Assyrians, Babylonians, Medes, and Persians..." (London, 1738-40). The drawing shows a seated male figure surrounded by Egyptian antiquities, including mummy cases, figurines, and a canopus jar; another figure stands before him, holding up a tablet, while pyramids, an obelisk, and a worshipper making an offering to the statue of a bull fill the ba…

artworks.title: Hannibal at Nine Years of Age Swearing Enmity to the Romans
artworks.medium: Red chalk and graphite with brown wash, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for an engraved illustration in Volume I of Charles Rollin's “The Ancient History of the Egyptians, Carthaginians, Assyrians, Babylonians, Medes, and Persians..." (London, 1738-40). Hannibal is shown as a boy alongside his father, placing a small sword on an altar below a statue of Hercules; two women are shown at left and additional figures fill the hall or temple in the background. It was presumably made for the third edition published by J. and P. Knapton i…

artworks.title: Venus on Clouds (left). Scene of Devastation (right)
artworks.medium: Graphite on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's sketches on this sheet are for two small title-page vignettes to Books I and II of “Della Nature delle Cose” by Titus Lucretius Carus (London, 1761). The study at left shows Venus reclining on a bed of clouds, with Cupid at left. The sketch at right shows an apparent massacre, with people fleeing over the fallen bodies of women and children. Gravelot's designs were engraved by Ferdinando Gregori (1743-1804)

artworks.title: Sappho Fainting at the Disappearance of Phaon's Ship
artworks.medium: Brush, black and gray wash over graphite, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: This sheet is Gravelot's preparatory design for an engraved illustration in A.M. Blin de Sainmore's "Lettre de Sapho à Phaon" (Paris, 1766). Sappho is shown swooning on the shore, supported by a female companion, as the ship carrying her lover Phaon sails away. The engraving after this drawing was executed by Jacques Aliamet (1726-1788). As Kraemer recorded, “There is a copy of Aliamet's engraving in the Morgan Library's 1806 edition of Ovid's Opera printed in Parma by Aloysius Mussi (Vol. I…

artworks.title: David Dancing before the Ark II
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink over indications in red chalk, on paper; partially traced with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is for an engraved headpiece intended for Book I of Le Franc de Pompignon's "Poésies Sacrées" (Paris : Chaubert, 1751). King David, as described in the biblical Books of Samuel, is shown with his harp, rejoicing at the head of a procession bearing the ark to Jerusalem. This is one of two preparatory drawings, along with 1968.15:11, for a headpiece vignette in the "Poésies Sacrées".

artworks.title: David Dancing before the Ark

artworks.title: Perseus, King of Macedon, in the Tent of the Roman Consul Paulus Emilius
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink and brown wash over graphite, on paper; incised with the stylus.
artworks.description: Gravelot's design is preparatory for an engraved frontispiece to Volume IX of Charles Rollin's "The Ancient History of the Egyptians, Carthaginians, Assyrians, Babylonians, Medes, and Persians..." (London, 1738-40). The 2nd century BC Roman consul and conqueror of Macedonia, Paulus Emilius, is shown seated in his tent, surrounded by soldiers; before him sits Perseus, his shoulders slumped in defeat. The engraving, signed "H. Gravelot inv.del. et sculp.", bears the date February 16, 1740.

artworks.description: Among Ernst's most important contributions to Surrealism are the drawings he created using the technique of frottage, as seen in this drawing. By placing a sheet of paper on an irregular surface--such as a wooden board, a leaf, of a piece of fabric--and rubbing it with a pencil, he obtained unexpected patterns that stimulated his imagination. "I was suprised by the sudden intensification of my visionary faculties and by the hallucinating succession of contradictory images," he recalled.

artworks.description: Best-known for his large-scale sculptures constructed of crushed automobile parts Chamberlain also explored two-dimensional media, such as photography, painting and drawing. artworks.title: Portrait of a Gentleman (Olaudah Equiano?)
artworks.medium: Black, brown and white chalk on gray-blue laid paper.
artworks.description: During his fellowship at the New York Public Library's Dorothy and Lewis B. Cullman Center, Michael Vazquez offered a compelling proposal regarding the identity of the sitter in this portrait. He suggested that this gripping image might depict the abolitionist and writer Olaudah Equiano (ca. 1745-1797). Born in what today is southern Nigeria, Equiano was captured and enslaved as a child. artworks.title: Study of a Junior Cavalry Officer Seated
artworks.medium: Graphite on paper.
artworks.description: Bazin notes that the present drawing must date between 1814 and 1820 because the young, smooth-shaven calvary officer wears a short jacket, the front panel of which after 1820 would become detachable. He wears a white cockade on his tall shako hat, a detail of his costume associated with the Restoration. artworks.title: Dancing Dogs with Musicians and Bystanders
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and umber wash over black chalk on paper.
artworks.description: The present sheet, one of a large group of finished independent drawings representing scenes of contemporary life. Here two musicians entertain a troupe of dancing dogs who imitate humans in their children's clothing and clumsy movement. A related drawing, featuring a group of Punchinellos with dancing dogs and surrounded by a crowd of equally humorous spectators, is in the Harvard University Art Museums (inv. no. 1965.421).

artworks.title: The Flight into Egypt
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and wash over black chalk on paper.
artworks.description: While there is no mention of the Holy Family crossing the river Jordan in the Gospels, the scene was frequently depicted in Venetian art; the conceit of showing the Holy Family's travel by boat perhaps coming naturally to Venetian artists. Examples include a painted version by Tiepolo himself from ca. 1767-70 (now in the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga, Lisbon), which is very similar to this drawn composition. Other versions of the subject are found in paintings, drawings, and prints by Giambat…

artworks.title: Head of the Virgin
artworks.medium: Pastel on paper.
artworks.description: Benedetto Luti was a masterful painter, collector, and draftsman in Rome at the turn of the eighteenth century. He is perhaps best known for his pastels of single heads and bust-length views of apostles, saints, angels, and children. Luti rendered these highly finished drawings such graceful intimacy and vibrant coloration that they stood as autonomous works rather than mere preparatory studies. artworks.title: Sheet of Studies
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink on laid paper; corners cut.
artworks.description: Perino del Vaga is one of the most inventive, influential and appealing draftsmen of the sixteenth century. A native of Florence, he apprenticed with Ridolfo Ghirlandaio and assiduously studied Michelangelo's Battle at Cascina cartoon -- the "school of the world" according the contemporary biographer Giorgio Vasari -- before joining Raphael's workshop in Rome around 1516. artworks.description: Best known for his paintings of nested squares in various colors called Homage to the Square, Josef Albers also produced a vast number of oil sketches, such as the present one, in which he experimented with color combinations. artworks.description: One of the pioneers of American Pop art, D'Arcangelo exhibited regularly in New York in the 1960s. Like his peers, Roy Lichtenstein and Andy Warhol, he derived his subjects and style from mass-media imagery. This rare drawing is related to his most famous series of paintings, which depict highways as seen from the driver's seat. artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and wash over graphite on laid paper, on a laid paper support inscribed in brown ink at center: S.F. no. 156.
artworks.description: This study derives from the series of grotesque heads by Leonardo da Vinci. Leonardo's original does not seem to survive, but a similar head can be found on a sheet attributed to Leonardo's close friend and follower Francesco Melzi, now in Windsor (RL 12493). Leonardo's original, featuring the same conical hat with the tuft of hair and two long plaits, is also recorded (in reverse) in an etching by Wenceslaus Hollar dated 1665. The present sketch seems to date from the sixteenth century and,…

artworks.title: Medium Word Drawing #30
artworks.medium: Ink on paper.
artworks.description: A prolific and highly versatile artist whose work - primarily sculptures and photographs - often defies classification, Samaras has produced works on paper throughout his career. The present sheet belongs to a series of drawings of single words Samaras created in the summer of 1975 using a hypodermic needle to apply the ink. Here the word DRAW is rendered in a scrawling, expressionistic fashion with a nervous cross-hatching pattern that gives the work a psychedelic quality.

artworks.description: Redon's human-faced arachnid exploits the potential of anthropomorphism to produce creatures that embody irrealism, a movement that countered the prevailing naturalism in literary Paris. Redon's work on his noirs was complex. He drew using various shades of black, erased, scratched out, sprayed with fixative, reworked, and manipulated the paper to produce a broad range of effects and tones despite the monochromatic media. artworks.title: The Tree Man
artworks.medium: Charcoal and graphite pencil on light brown paper.
artworks.description: This enigmatic depiction of a tree set in barren landscape, the trunk of which also serves as a neck supporting a man's head, is typical of the fantastic hybrids Redon conjured in his charcoal drawings. From his earliest years, Redon was interested in giving visual form to the subconscious. Sympathetic mentors were critical to Redon's development: Rodolphe Bresdin encouraged him to use his imagination, and botanist Armand Clauvaud fed his fascination with the mysteries of the natural world. artworks.title: Saint Lawrence
artworks.medium: Graphite and brown wash on paper.
artworks.description: Maella was one of the most successful Spanish artists employed at the court of Bourbon kings Charles III and Charles IV. This sheet depicts St. Lawrence, who was burned alive. Flanked by two angels, the saint ascends on a cloud in the center of the composition holding a grill, symbolic of his martyrdom. The drawing is squared for transfer, indicating its preparatory function for a larger painting. --Exhibition Label, from "Visions and Nightmares: Four Centuries of Spanish Drawings"

His depiction of the Virgin and child sleeping between the paws of a monumental sculpted sphinx set in the desert debuted at the Salon of 1879 and captured the public's imagination. In the years leading up to his masterwork, Merson explored the nocturnal theme numerous times, reworking the composition in each version. artworks.description: Born and trained in Dublin, Buck eventually moved to London, where his elegant portrait drawings were in high demand. He also produced a large number of decorative fashion plates, which may explain the refined Neoclassicism apparent in this portrait of the nine youngest of the twelve children of Richard Bagot (1782-1854), who in 1825 was a canon of Windsor and later became bishop of Bath and Wells. -- Exhibition Label, from "Life Lines: Portrait Drawings from Dürer to Picasso."

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.medium: Graphite pencil and beeswax on paper.
artworks.description: In this early drawing, Marden combined graphite with beeswax to achieve a rich, saturated surface. The work shows Marden at the crossroads between the two tendencies that dominated artistic production in the United States during the 1960s: the legacy of Abstract Expressionism and the primacy of Minimalism. Although the reduced palette and exploration of geometric shapes relate to the Minimalist aesthetic, the gestural quality of the worked surface evokes an Abstract Expressionist approach.

artworks.title: Campbell's Soup Can and Dollar Bills
artworks.medium: Graphite pencil and watercolor on paper.
artworks.description: By 1960, Warhol was a successful commercial artist known primarily for his designs for shoe advertisements. Wishing to move from commercial to fine art, he adopted the free, gestural style of the Abstract Expressionists. This drawing belongs to the brief, early Pop period during which Warhol applied this style to images of consumer culture. Soon after, he began using the silkscreen technique that would become the hallmark of his work.

artworks.title: Passacaglia
artworks.medium: Pen and brush and ink, watercolor and opaque watercolor, oil paint, crayon, and graphite pencil, with scratching and selectively applied glaze on paperboard prepared with white ground.
artworks.description: Associated with the Abstract Expressionist movement, Pousette-Dart produced an important body of works on paper in the early 1940s in which he explored complex techniques to create mysterious and evocative semi-abstract imagery. Combining a free application of color with exacting calligraphic details and an intricate layering of mediums, Passacaglia--whose title evokes dance rhythm--is an example of these works that test the border between painting and drawing.

artworks.title: The Martyrdom of Saint Agatha
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and wash over black chalk on laid paper.
artworks.description: The study is preparatory for Baglione's altarpiece of the Martydom of Saint Agatha, now in the National Museum of Fine Arts in Valletta, Malta. There are a number of changes between the compositional sketch and the finished work, but this is fairly typical for Baglione. A number of common details -- the action of binding the saint, the semi-recumbent figure at lower left -- point to the connection between the drawing and painting, and the painting is Baglione's only work with this subject.

artworks.description: Speller worked as a sharecropper in the Mississippi Delta region before relocating to Memphis in 1939. artworks.title: Faith
artworks.medium: Graphite, black chalk, white opaque watercolor on wove paper.
artworks.description: Gemito produced this drawing as part of a design competition for a monument to Pope Pius X installed above a doorway in St. Peter's Basilica. This is one of several studies for the figure of Faith (see also Milan, Collezione d'arte della Fondazione Cariplo), which would have appeared in the lower section. Gemito did not ultimately secure the commission, but the figure's upturned face and fervent gaze suggest the spiritual intensity intended in the monument.

artworks.description: Although he began his career as a painter, Taylor turned to sculpture and drawing in the mid-1980s. During his short life he produced more than 5,000 drawings, which, while related to his three-dimensional constructions by their subjects, form an independent body of work of great sensuousness and painterliness. The present drawing belongs to what Taylor referred to as the Swahili Time group, inspired by a 1980 trip to Africa that marked a turning point in his career. Fascinated with the conce…

artworks.title: Study for a Dancer Adjusting Her Bodice
artworks.medium: Charcoal on paper.
artworks.description: By the late 1880s, charcoal was Degas' preferred medium for studies of nude models; he repeatedly explored certain figures and poses in groups of dynamically interrelated drawings. In this sheet a ballet dancer lifts her arms to adjust her bodice; a clothed figure in the same pose appears in a number of the artist's pastels from ca. 1897.

artworks.title: The Blood of Christ Redeems the World
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and white opaque watercolor over black chalk, squared in black chalk on paper.
artworks.description: Benso was the leading Baroque painter in Genoa in the middle of the seventeenth century, but he also painted many works for the Imperial Abbey of St. Martin at Weingarten in Southern Germany. This drawing, one of his greatest, is a preparatory study for the high altar of the monastery church. It is the first work by the artist to enter the Morgan collection.

artworks.title: Adoration of the Magi
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink, brown wash, and white opaque watercolor, over black chalk, on paper; squared for transfer.
artworks.description: This striking, large-scale sheet is an excellent example of the Caravaggesque manner which dominated Bloemaert's artistic output during the 1620s. Over the course of this decade, the artist often returned to the subject of the Adoration of the Magi, which allowed for the creation of busy, complex compositions, at which he excelled. This drawing might have been preparatory for a painting commissioned for the Jesuit church in Brussels, now at the Musée de Grenoble. Watermark: Shield with three…

artworks.title: Seated Figure of St. John the Evangelist in a Spandrel. Verso: A Ceiling Decoration, and Studies of Standing and Seated Figures
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink on paper.
artworks.description: One of the most impressive drawings by Perino del Vaga, the recto of this large sheet features a vigorous sketch for a spandrel with Saint John the Evangelist. Both it and the ceiling design on the verso include Perino's typically mannered, elegant figures and probably relate to a commission from the 1540s, when he was arguably the leading painter active in Rome. Watermark: Lamb with standard inside circle, (Agnus Dei, Paschal lamb). Watermark, beta radiograph. lamb, pennant, standard, circle…

artworks.title: The Battle of Otto von Wittelsbach and Henry the Lion
artworks.medium: Pen and black ink and wash, and watercolor, over black chalk, on paper; squared in red chalk.
artworks.description: Peter Candid belonged to a group of itinerant artists with Northern roots but Italian experience and training, active in the Bavarian court in Munich. One of his primary responsibilities was the designing and planning for the execution of sumptuous tapestries used for decorating the royal residence. This drawing is a study for one in a series of ten tapestries celebrating the accomplishments of the founder of the Bavarian line, Otto von Wittelsbach. The tapestry, which reproduces the design i…

artworks.title: The Israelites Fleeing Egypt
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink, over black chalk, on paper.
artworks.description: Naldini trained with Jacopo Pontormo and spent most of his career in his native Florence, where he was amont the founders of the Accademia del Disegno. This sheet, however, is from a sketchbook he filled during a trip to Rome in the early 1560s. Executed in Naldini's characteristic vigorous penwork, it records a lost fresco by Polidoro da Caravaggio.

artworks.title: Design for a Medal Celebrating the Order of St. Stephen
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink, brown wash, in an inscribed circle; laid down on an eighteenth-century mount.
artworks.description: Preparatory for one of the fourteen bronze medals commemorating the deeds of Cosimo I de' Medici, Grand Duke of Tuscany, this drawing is devoted to Cosimo's creation of the Holy Military Order of Saint Stephen. It shows a novice knight kneeling before an ancient altar and swearing allegiance to Cosimo, while he is presented with the Maltese cross and a ceremonial sword. As apparent in this drawing, Zucchi's early style of draftsmanship owes much to Giorgio Vasari, whose exaggerated anatomical…

This small pastel is a study for Vuillard's painting on the theme…

artworks.title: Palace Interior with Tritons and Mirrored Gallery, a Design for the Stage
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and black wash, over black chalk, on paper.
artworks.description: While the best-known Bibiena sets evoke the courtyards of majestic Baroque palaces, the artists also followed contemporary architectural trends. This design suggests a grand Parisian hotel interior, with a unified arrangement of chairs, side tables, and pier mirrors in a room decorated with paintings of gods and goddesses. The sheet may have been executed when Carlo Bibiena was assisting his father, Giuseppe Bibiena, at the Margravial Opera House in Bayreuth around 1750.

artworks.title: Left Portion of a Palatial Hall, a Design for the Stage
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and wash, over graphite, on paper.
artworks.description: This remarkable working drawing illustrates various stages of the creative process. A graphite underdrawing provided the precise perspective before the artist fluidly rendered the architectural surface ornament of festoons and scrolls in pen and ink. The design also includes notations that suggest how it would be realized in the three-dimensional space of the theater: letters corresponding to different scenery flats that would have come together to create the appearance of a unified stage set…

artworks.title: Stage Design with Sailing Vessels
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and wash, over graphite, on paper.
artworks.description: An inscription on the back of this sheet reveals that it was a design for Vivaldi's opera La Cunegonda, performed during carnival in Mantua in 1718, when Francesco served as the impresario of the Teatro Comico. As the final setting for the opera, the imposing ships, lit from behind, would have left a strong impression.

artworks.title: Entryway Leading to a Courtyard and Two Levels of Galleries, a Design for the Stage
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink, gray wash, and blue watercolor, incised, on paper.
artworks.description: Although the Bibienas were most famous for their innovative scena per angolo (scene viewed at an angle) stage designs, they also continued to design sets with a central vanishing point, like that used here. An illuminated atrium with densely colonnaded galleries was a motif favored by Giuseppe Bibiena.

artworks.title: A Colonnaded Stage
artworks.medium: Pen and brown and black ink, and gray wash, on paper.
artworks.description: This drawing by Carlo Bibiena dates to early in his career, perhaps to around 1750 when he was assisting his father, Giuseppe, at the Margravial Opera House in Bayreuth. The architectural structure exemplifies Carlo's formal, restrained draftsmanship; unusually, however, work continued on the sheet even after the highly finished framework was complete. Festoons were added atop the proscenium and columns, and ghostly scrolls were sketched on some of the plinths at left. Fragments of paper atta…

artworks.title: Three-Story Atrium with Caryatids
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink, over leadpoint, on paper.

artworks.title: Stage Set: Palace Courtyard with Columns and Statues
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and gray wash, over graphite, on paper.
artworks.description: A courtyard scena per angolo (scene viewed at an angle) could suggest an expansive palace without depicting the entire structure. The repetition of a few groups of columns prompts the viewer to imagine dozens more, just out of view. Even in the relatively small scale of a drawing, the immersive monumentality is palpable. The drawing is unusual in that it shows alternate schemes, one with and one without a proscenium arch framing the view.

artworks.title: Stage Set: Grand Palace Hall with Columns and Grand Staircase
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and gray wash, over graphite, on paper.
artworks.description: Extraordinary in its range of detail and subtle wash shading, this drawing was probably executed by one of Ferdinando Bibiena's pupils at the Accademia Clementina in Bologna. A quintessential example of the scena per angolo (scene viewed at an angle), the drawing retains prick marks and inscribed lines that show the careful development of its multiviewpoint perspective.

artworks.title: Courtyard of a Palace, a Design for the Stage
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink, gray wash, and blue watercolor, over graphite, on paper.

artworks.title: Entrance to a Palace with Colonnade and Figures
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and gray wash, over graphite(?), on paper.
artworks.description: This sheet retains traces of an underdrawing that reveals the careful attention paid to an accurate projection of the perspective. Bibiena sets would not have included painted figures, so this drawing might record a live production (perhaps as a preparatory study for a commemorative engraving). Alternately, it could be an independent drawing exercise.

artworks.title: Fisherman Pulling in Their Boats, Le Havre
artworks.medium: Brown ink wash over graphite on wove paper.

artworks.title: Study of a Candlestick
artworks.medium: Black chalk on tan paper
artworks.description: From 1876 onward Bonvin was housebound due to illness. Turning to domestic subjects such as coffee grinders and candlesticks, he lavished care on these depictions of everyday items. Here, spent matches accumulate at the candleʼs base, suggesting the passage of time as poignantly as the smoke curls of the just-extinguished flame. Bonvin made multiple drawings of the same objects, and their serial numbering on the lower left suggests that he intended to publish them.

artworks.title: A Breton Peasant Woman with a Fishing Net, Standing by the Sea
artworks.medium: Black chalk on blue-gray laid paper
artworks.description: Watermark: Michellet. Bretonʼs art, with its focus on women laborers, reflects his origins in the rural town of Courrières in northern France. On later visits to Douarnenez, a fishing community in Brittany, Breton was struck by the monumentality not only of its landscape but of its people. He drew and painted portraits of villagers -- such as this fisherwoman paused in her work -- whom he considered Michelangelesque figures in modern dress.

artworks.title: Study for “Commerce Uniting the Peoples: Eastern Merchants at a Western Port"
artworks.medium: Graphite, colored pencils (red, blue and yellow) on wove paper
artworks.description: Chassériau was born in Spanish-held Santo Domingo to parents of French and Haitian descent. A precocious student, he trained with Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres but soon felt the influence of Eugène Delacroix. After an initial voyage to Algeria in 1846, he began exploring North African subjects in his work, including in his designs for six murals adorning Parisʼs Cour des Comptes, or Court of Audit. The monumental scheme was devoted to the glory of France in peace and wartime, with the forme…

artworks.title: Landscape with Two Trees
artworks.medium: Charcoal and black chalk on laid paper
artworks.description: Beginning in the 1850s, Corot experimented with cliché-verre, or "glass plate," a reproductive print that is a hybrid of drawing, printmaking, and photography. He was tutored in the method by photographer Adalbert Cuvelier, an originator of cliché-verre in France and father of Eugène, who in turn taught the technique to Daubigny, Huet, Millet, and Rousseau. The process involves coating a glass plate in printerʼs ink or photographic emulsion, scratching a linear image into the coating, and…

artworks.title: Moonlit Landscape
artworks.medium: Charcoal, stumped and scratched, with white chalk and overall fixative on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: Corot exploited the potential of charcoalʼs velvety deep blackness to convey the vague forms of trees as the eye would perceive them after adjusting to the darkness of a nocturnal walk. Such sheets continue the Romantic taste for moonlit landscapes and prefigure the sense of mystery conjured by dark media in the hands of Symbolist Odilon Redon (1840-1916).

metadata.credit_line: Gift of Karen B. Cohen in Honor of Colin B. Bailey.

artworks.title: River Landscape (recto), Untitled (verso)
artworks.medium: Charcoal with smudging and locally applied fixative on wove paper
artworks.description: Corotʼs late, soft style reveals his affinity for photography and the effects it could achieve. Admiring the mediumʼs monochromatic tonal scale, he muted his palette beginning in the 1850s. Here, the indistinct edges of the foliage evoke the way stirring leaves blurred during long exposures. Moreover, his softening of background elements reflects the impact of photographyʼs single focus.

artworks.title: Trees in the Forest of Fontainebleau
artworks.medium: Graphite on laid paper
artworks.description: Corot was part of a core group of artists who began visiting Fontainebleau as early as the 1820s and 1830s, laying the groundwork for the thriving artistic community that would develop in Barbizon by midcentury. Here, his Neoclassical idealism is offset by a detailed attention to nature; he imposes order and an organized pattern within the organic form of the treetops. A faint groundline at the bottom of the sheet gives a sense of the treesʼ majestic scale. The silvery graphite and delicacy o…

artworks.title: Study for the Head of the Poet in The Thorny Path
artworks.medium: Black chalk on blue laid paper
artworks.description: In his 1873 painting "A Thorny Path," Couture skewered French society using the motif of a triumphal procession. A bare-breasted courtesan drives her chariot down a path lined with brambles; the vehicle is led by four captive men: a bacchic reveler, a dreamy young troubadour, a pensive poet, and a resigned soldier. An older woman sits in the back of the carriage, looking out at the viewer. The canvas in the Philadelphia Museum of Art is a metaphor for what the artist perceived as a decadent c…

artworks.title: Pierrot Before the Judge
artworks.medium: Black and white chalk on gray-green paper
artworks.description: Using his paintings as a vehicle for satirical commentary, Couture produced a series featuring Pierrot and Harlequin, stock characters from the commedia dellʼarte, a popular theatrical form with origins in Italy. Here, the downcast Pierrot is on trial for having stolen wine and game (at center) from the innkeeper and chef (at left). As Pierrotʼs lawyer, Harlequin advocates passionately on his clientʼs behalf, unwittingly leaning forward to reveal the blunt cudgel he has stashed beneath his ro…

artworks.title: Self Portrait
artworks.medium: Black chalk, white chalk on blue laid paper, faded, lined overall to modern wove paper.
artworks.description: After at least six failed attempts to win the Rome Prize, which allowed French artists to study in the Italian capital, Couture rejected the academic path and forged an independent career. His exceptional skill as a draftsman was essential to his many large canvases, such as Romans of the Decadence, which caused a sensation at the 1847 Paris Salon. Couture described himself as a "militant and aggressive personality" and was proud that his self-portraits conveyed as much. This intimate example…

artworks.title: Cattle and Figures in the Moonlight
artworks.medium: Black chalk with smudging and erasures on laid paper
artworks.description: Daubigny was lauded for his sincerity, achieved by copying nature not through the eye and hand but "with his soul," as his disciples said. This drawing of cows grazing and figures shearing sheep at night was created in preparation for a painting. Nocturnes became a theme for Daubigny, whose moonlit scenes grew increasingly moody in his later years.

metadata.credit_line: Gift of Karen B. Cohen in Honor of William M. Griswold.

artworks.title: The Meadow at Graves, near Villerville
artworks.medium: Black chalk, with graphite on laid paper
artworks.description: Daubignyʼs commitment to working outdoors, on land or from a boat, was much admired by the younger generation of artists who would come to be known as Impressionists. Le Pré des Graves is a meadow in the coastal community of Villerville in Calvados, Normandy, near where the Impressionists began to work in the 1870s. Daubigny found its forms alluring and depicted the windswept trees and long grasses in paintings and etchings, in daylight and moonlight, during the years 1874-75.

artworks.title: View of Le Rageur under a stormy sky, Fontainebleau
artworks.artist: Narcisse Virgile Diaz de la Peña
artworks.medium: Watercolor, opaque watercolor, pen and brown ink on wove paper
artworks.description: Before he fell under the influence of Rousseau and followed him into the forest of Fontainebleau, Diaz decorated porcelain and painted sentimental figures. In Fontainebleau, he shifted his focus to the wild, untouched parts of the forest, recognizing that nature contained a drama of its own. Diazʼs commercial success as a landscape painter allowed him to extend aid to fellow Barbizon artists like Millet and Rousseau. artworks.title: A Peasant Leading a Horse-Drawn Cart
artworks.medium: Graphite on laid paper
artworks.description: In April 1820, Géricault traveled to London to exhibit his dramatic masterpiece "Raft of the Medusa." He would remain in London for twenty months, returning to Paris in December 1821. He traveled there with his friend, the artist Nicolas-Toussaint Charlet, who is credited with opening Géricault's eyes to the plight of the London poor. While in London, Géricault was part of the social circle of the horse dealer Adam Elmore (1784-1849) and his French wife Zoé. In his works from this period,…

artworks.title: Sketches of Five Heads of Men Wearing Turbans
artworks.medium: Pen and iron gall ink on reverse of an autograph letter in brown ink.
artworks.description: Géricault often used the paper he had at hand for sketches; in this case, it was a sheet with a note to an unknown recipient. Written in the early 1820s, he mentions that his health has improved. The sheet contains five head studies of men wearing turbans. The lower three studies feature a sitter with a broad mustache, no beard, and thick eyebrows. This man is almost certainly Mustapha Sassen, a Tunisian Arab whom Géricault hired as a manservant in 1817 and who lived with him until 1821. Mu…

artworks.title: Studies after Rubens' The Last Judgement
artworks.medium: Graphite on wove paper
artworks.description: After a year in Italy, Géricault returned to Paris in the autumn of 1817. The impact of studying Michelangelo's Last Judgment and the challenge of developing a composition with many dynamic figures likely inspired the artist to turn to Peter Paul Rubens' "Small Last Judgment" of 1619 (Alte Pinakothek, Munich). Géricault knew Rubens' composition through Jonas Suyderhoef's 1642 reproductive print "The Fall of the Damned," and it is from the print that he copied passages in 1817-18. Lorenz Eit…

artworks.title: Portrait of Auguste Brunet and Studies of a hand and leg after the Raft of the Medusa
artworks.medium: Iron gall ink on wove paper
artworks.description: This sheet curiously juxtaposes a portrait study with an image of a hand and leg based on figures in Géricault's Raft of the Medusa, which debuted at the Salon of 1819. The hand is that of the young man at the right of the raft near the front who reaches forward to hoist himself up by grasping the thigh of the man in front of him, who, supported by barrels, waves a white cloth. The leg is that of the black man at the apex of the raft who steps up onto a barrel with the support of a man with…

artworks.title: Head of King Clovis
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink on laid paper
artworks.description: In 1812 Gros was commissioned to decorate the central dome of the Panthéon with a program that celebrated four leading dynasties in France: Clovis, Charlemagne, Louis IX, and Napoleon. Through the realization of this commission, we can trace the vicissitudes of the decade. With the restoration of the Bourbon Monarchy in 1814, he began work on the frescoes, replacing Napoleon with Louis XVIII. When Napoleon returned for the 100 Days in 1815, the canvas was swapped but again removed following…

artworks.title: The Death of Alcestis, or The Heroism of Conjugal Love
artworks.medium: Black chalk with smudging, white chalk, both chalks worked wet, on two vertically joined sheets of machine made laid paper.
artworks.description: The French Revolution and subsequent conflicts popularized themes of virtue and sacrifice, often derived from Greco-Roman sources. This drawing dramatically envisions Euripidesʼs early tragedy Alcestis (438 BC), which also provided the basis for contemporary operas. In the play, the Fates permit the condemned King Admetus to live if a volunteer takes his place in death. As Admetusʼs elderly father demurs, his young wife, Queen Alcestis, steps forward to sacrifice her life so her children will…

artworks.title: Lake in Compiègne Forest
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink and wash on beige laid paper
artworks.description: Like Fontainebleau, Compiègne forest had served as a royal hunting ground for centuries.This early, large-scale drawing by Huet explores the motif of the lake as a mirror for the surrounding forest. Compiègne was the seat of the Orléans family, who owned a chateau there, and Huet served as the drawing master to the Duchesse dʼOrléans. Her husband, Duke Ferdinand Philippe, was a draftsman and landscape painter as well as a patron of Huet.

artworks.title: Study for "Forest of Fontainebleau: Hunters"
artworks.medium: Black chalk, brown and gray wash, opaque lead white watercolor on blue wove paper, altered to green-blue.
artworks.description: As the leading Romantic artist of the 1820s, Huet shaped landscape painting for a generation and was a dominant influence on the Barbizon school. He started painting in the Forest of Fontainebleau in 1849 and returned frequently. Fontainebleau and its sister forest of Compiègne had served as royal hunting preserves for centuries and were revived as such by Napoleon III in the nineteenth century. Huet created this drawing as a preparatory study for a painting now in the Louvre, Forest of Font…

artworks.title: Seated Cavalier
artworks.medium: Graphite, white chalk, black wash on laid paper.
artworks.description: Before becoming Napoleonʼs official painter of military exploits, Meissonier produced genre scenes with figures dressed in eighteenth-century costume. This is one of two large-scale studies in the Cohen gift that is preparatory for a miniature-scale painted composition depicting two men discussing the Siege of Bergen op Zoom, a 1747 maneuver in which the French army captured the Dutch town. artworks.title: Studies of a Young Boy Tumbling
artworks.medium: Graphite with smudging on wove paper.
artworks.description: The Berlin-based Menzel repeatedly visited Verona in the 1880s, always with a sketchbook at hand. The busy marketplace -- the cityʼs center since the Roman era -- is the subject of his 1884 painting Piazza delle Erbe. In the painting, a rambunctious boy almost somersaults into a woman; she is saved from the collision by her husbandʼs umbrella. Here, Menzelʼs quick graphite marks capture the acrobatics of Max Schenk, the boy who modeled for the artist.

artworks.medium: Charcoal, black chalk with overall fixative on wove paper.
artworks.description: In contrast to many of his Parisian contemporaries who were looking to the countryside for inspiration and drawing specific trees, swamps, and gorges, Redonʼs greatest resource was his imagination, from which he plucked elements assembled with the logic of dreams. He wrote that working from nature left him depleted and that he was rejuvenated only by revisiting the experience in his mind and depicting his recollections. While landscapes enlivened with small-scale figures are a common and trad…

artworks.title: Cliffs in Normandy
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink on laid paper
artworks.description: Rousseau visited Normandy in 1831, following in the footsteps of the watercolorists of the previous generation. His pen lines here are so daring and free that some have suggested the view is a later remembrance of these coastal cliffs drawn in the 1850s. The quivering contours and scribbled shading lends a sense of speed to the composition, as though the sky or weather were rapidly changing. It was this type of mark making that elicited Vincent van Goghʼs appreciation for Rousseauʼs drawings.

artworks.title: Study of Trees in the Forest at Fontainebleau
artworks.medium: Black and white chalk on blue laid paper, faded to brown
artworks.description: Rousseau found spirituality in nature, seeing himself as its interpreter. He wrote to a friend, "I also hear the voices of the trees. The surprises of their movements, their variety of forms, and their singular attraction toward the light suddenly revealed to me the language of the forest. This entire world of flora lived as mutes whose signs I divined and whose passions I discovered." A supporter of forest preservation, Rousseau advocated for a passive approach that was at odds with forestry…

artworks.title: Waterfall in the Auvergne; verso: Sketch of rocky terrain
artworks.medium: Black chalk on laid paper
artworks.description: At the age of eighteen, after failing to pass even the first stage of competition for the coveted Prix de Rome at the École des Beaux-Arts, Rousseau fled not to Italy but to Franceʼs Auvergne region. For six months he dedicated himself to studying and rendering nature -- the textures of tree bark, rock formations, flowing water, and waving grasses. This period was critical in shaping his artistic approach.

artworks.description: Among Rousseauʼs collection of seventeenth-century Dutch prints was a stellar impression of Rembrandtʼs "The Three Trees," an etching well known and often copied in France. It provided the inspiration for this composition with a similarly strong foreground. Rousseau experimented with Rembrandtʼs practice of placing a dark form against a bright clear sky but tempered the silhouette by playing with the fall of light on the treetops and by adding hints of color. artworks.description: This delicate portrait was drawn early in Seuratʼs career when he was a pupil of Henri Lehmann at the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris. The young artist became frustrated with the conservative curriculum and would soon develop his distinctive monochromatic drawing style. Here, the twenty-year-old Seurat has likely portrayed the forty-nine-year-old Camille Pissarro, a father figure to French avant-garde artists in the 1870s.
